checks.claim: C1/G1 source identification: Teschl 2014 second edition (GSM157, ISBN 978-1-4704-1704-8). Thm 10.2 p258, conditional Thm 10.13 p273 and max-min Thm 4.12 pp140-141 are stated with the hypotheses the target uses.
checks.reason: The title page shows SECOND EDITION and GSM vol. 157. The copyright page shows the ISBN and (c) 2009, 2014. Thm 10.2: real V in L^inf_inf + L2 for n<=3 is relatively compact w.r.t. H0, so H=H0+V on H2 is self-adjoint and bounded below, sigma_ess=[0,inf), and C_c^inf is a core. V=-bU (bounded, compact support) qualifies. Thm 10.13 reads 'If E0=min sigma(H) is an eigenvalue, it is simple and the eigenfunction is strictly positive', so it is conditional, as the target says. Thm 4.12 defines E_n as inf sigma_ess once eigenvalues run out, and p141 permits the quadratic form domain. The target attributes no uniformity to Teschl.

checks.claim: G1 bounds: -b1||U||inf <= E1(b) <= -eps, E1<E2<=0, |Ej(b)-Ej(c)| <= ||U||inf |b-c|, gap Delta>0, l<=lambda_b<=L, lambda_b-mu_b>=d0.
checks.reason: Because U>=0, <w,H_b w> <= int|grad w|^2 - b0 int U w^2 <= -eps for all b>=b0, so E1<=-eps<0=inf sigma_ess. This makes E1 an isolated eigenvalue, after which 10.13 gives simplicity and an a.e.-positive eigenfunction. The lower bound is H_b >= -b||U||inf. E2 is either an eigenvalue different from E1 (by simplicity) or the threshold 0>E1. The Lipschitz bound follows from H_c - ||U|||b-c| <= H_b <= H_c + ||U|||b-c| and form monotonicity (Cor. 4.13, same page p141). Delta>0 holds because E2-E1 is continuous and positive on compact K. The rate gap follows from lambda-mu = (E2-E1)/(lambda+mu) >= Delta/(2 sqrt(b1||U||inf)). No second bound state is presupposed and mu_b=0 is allowed.

checks.claim: G1 continuity: b -> p_b continuous in L2 and H2, with no p_b in L1 and no 1D ODE.
checks.reason: This is feasible. The Riesz projection around the isolated simple E1 is norm-continuous in b, since H_b-H_c is bounded and the gap is uniform. Positivity fixes the sign of the normalized eigenvector. H2 continuity follows from Delta p_b = -(E1(b)+bU)p_b. None of this needs L1 or tail bounds.

checks.claim: C2/G2: with e_b^E=(p_b,lambda_b p_b) and ell_b^E=(<p_b,v>+<p_b,z>/lambda_b)/2, the bound ||P_b^E(t)Q_b^E|| <= C(1+t)e^{mu_b t} holds uniformly. Only the growing branch is removed; the decaying branch is kept.
checks.reason: On the ground mode, a''=lambda^2 a has the growing branch (p,lambda p) and the decaying branch (p,-lambda p). ell^E gives 1 on the first and 0 on the second, and the pairing with z in H^{-1/2} is legitimate because p_b is in H2, a subset of H^{1/2}. The old d1 method's fractional comparison (B<=A_b<=cB with form domain H1, resolvent and square-root integral) is dimension-free. Its scalar wave-entry bounds on [-mu^2,inf), including mu=0 via S_t(0)=t, and its Picard/Gronwall identification with the Duhamel flow carry over to R^d. The target correctly labels that note as a d1 METHOD to be re-proved, not an all-dimensional theorem.

checks.claim: C3/G3: block form P_b(t)(e,c) = (P^E e + K_b(t)c, C(t)c) with K_b(t)c = int_0^t P^E(t-r) D_b C(r)c dr and D_b c=(0,bU c1).
checks.reason: This matches the accepted note's Section 7 deterministic base with h=bU, g=0, and its B(b)(e,c)=(0,b(e1+c1)) map from F to E. The constant coordinates evolve by (c1+tc2, c2) as in note (1) and (8).

checks.claim: G3 constant functional: f_b = b int U p_b/(2 lambda_b), and ell_b = ell^E + f_b(c1/lambda + c2/lambda^2) gives ell_b(e_b)=1, ell_b P_b(t) = e^{lambda t} ell_b and P Pi = Pi P = e^{lambda t} Pi.
checks.reason: Hand check of the generator: ell^E(0,bUc1) = f_b c1, so f c1 + alpha c2 = lambda alpha c1 + lambda beta c2, giving alpha=f/lambda and beta=f/lambda^2. Direct check with the block formula: ell^E K(t)c = e^{lambda t} f(c1/lambda+c2/lambda^2) - f(c1+tc2)/lambda - f c2/lambda^2. Adding the constant part gives exactly e^{lambda t} ell_b(0,c). So Pi_b is a bounded rank-one projection and both commutation identities follow.

checks.claim: G3 positivity: inf_K ell_b(e0) > 0 and inf_K O_phi(e_b) > 0, with continuity and uniform bounds of e_b, ell_b, Pi_b.
checks.reason: ell_b(e0) = f_b/lambda_b. Here int U p_b > 0 because U is continuous, nonnegative and nonzero and p_b>0 a.e. O_phi(e_b) = int phi p_b > 0. Both are continuous in b, which gives uniform positivity on compact K. Only a.e. positivity tested against integrals is used; no point trace and no p_b in L1.

checks.claim: C4/G4: ||P_b Q_b|| <= C(1+t)^3 e^{mu t}, the normalized exp-gap bound for any eta < inf(lambda-mu), and finite-T Lipschitz dependence on b. Is a desired complement bound assumed circularly?
checks.reason: Derived without circularity from G2 plus the explicit forcing. P Q (e,0) = P^E Q^E e. On constants: the Q^E-forcing part is bounded by int_0^t C(1+t-r)e^{mu(t-r)}(1+r)dr <= C(1+t)^3 e^{mu t}, including mu=0. The Pi^E-forcing part minus the subtracted e^{lambda t}ell_b(0,c)e_b equals -f_b((c1+tc2)/lambda + c2/lambda^2)e_b^E, which is polynomial. The exp-gap bound uses lambda-mu >= d0 and lambda >= l. The b-Lipschitz bound comes from Duhamel with the bounded difference (b-c)U on [0,T0]. It is correctly stated as parameter continuity, not operator-norm time continuity.

checks.claim: C5/G5: Q(g) is finite and strictly positive; U_R = m_R(Gamma*q) is smooth, compact and nonzero; int U_R g^2 = Q(g); for any b0>0, a finite R and a psi_L trial give a common negative trial with C_G = c0^2 2^{alpha-d} Gamma(B1) int q and q fixed.
checks.reason: Gamma is nonzero and homogeneous, so Gamma(B_r) = r^{d-alpha} Gamma(B1) > 0 for every r. It therefore charges every neighbourhood of 0. Combined with q*q~(0) = int q^2 > 0, this gives Q(g) > 0; finiteness follows from Radon local finiteness. Gamma*q is smooth because Gamma is locally finite and q is in C_c^inf. Since m_R=1 on supp g, int U_R g^2 = int (Gamma*q) q = Q(g). Trial: psi_L^2 >= c0^2 L^{-d} on B_L. Tonelli gives int_{B_L} Gamma*q = int q(y) Gamma(B_L - y) dy, and |y| <= A <= L/2 gives B_{L/2} inside B_L - y. The constant C_G as stated follows, with int q = 1. The kinetic term is Dpsi L^{-2}, and alpha < 2 because a > 0, so the potential term L^{-alpha} dominates. This covers singular invariant-direction Gamma and the white endpoint alpha=d=1. Quantifiers are correct: R depends only on (Gamma, q, psi, b0) and is fixed before asymptotics. No all-strength binding claim and no change of q.

The JSON values match my hand formulas: entrance beta/(2 lambda^2) and wrong-projection defect beta/(2 lambda), e.g. lambda=2, beta=1 gives 1/8 and 1/4; lambda=3, beta=3 gives 1/6 and 1/2. Its potential (1/L) int phi^2 phi(x/L)^2 is consistent with Gamma = delta x Leb^2 (alpha=1, a=0.5), and its sign change between L=64 and L=256 is arithmetically consistent. It is labelled as 35/60-digit agreement, not a certificate.

The G1 Lipschitz bound follows most directly from form monotonicity (Teschl Cor. 4.13, on the viewed p141) together with the max-min definition. Citing 4.13 alongside 4.12 would make the import exact.
The exponent (1+t)^3 in G4 is a valid but non-sharp bound (the derivation gives t(1+t)^2). This is harmless.
The '432 residual differential/initial identities' count is 432 differential checks; the initial-value identity is asserted only in the 108 t=0 iterations. The wording slightly merges the two.

check-fixed-profile-trial.py uses psi=g0 (a product bump). It is supported in B2, but it has no positive lower bound c0 on all of B1 (it vanishes as |x_j| -> 1). It illustrates the fixed-q mechanism, but it does not literally instantiate the G5 psi route. Using B_{1/2}, or a psi bounded below on B1, would align the two.

G5 should say explicitly that Gamma(B1) > 0 follows from Gamma nonzero plus homogeneity (any charged ball B_r gives Gamma(B1) = r^{alpha-d} Gamma(B_r) > 0). The target asks for this to be verified but does not display the argument.
The match between G1-G4 and the inputs of the abstract moving-block cone cannot be verified from the packet. The downstream gate should check it against the cone note.
